prompt: A survey asks only visitors who stayed until the end of a long event whether its length was appropriate. Explain how this selection could distort the result. A response of around 80 words is enough.
text: This creates **survivorship bias**: people who left early—possibly because the event was too long, boring, or tiring—are excluded. Those who stayed until the end are more likely to have tolerated or preferred the event’s length, so their answers may make the event seem more appropriately timed than it really was. The survey therefore cannot represent all visitors, especially those most negatively affected by the event’s duration.
